Self.Wiki: An enemy spawner. It reuses its own listed enemies: when one is dead (or still held back), the generator waits a random interval, picks a batch size, then warps that enemy to one of its spawn regions and revives it. It repeats while it is enabled and below its limits. Event scripts control it by Entity ID with EMEVD Set Generator State (enable or disable) and EMEVD Invoke Enemy Generator (spawn a batch now).

MaxNum.Wiki: The most of this generator's enemies that may be alive at once. No batch starts while this many are alive, and a batch is cut short to stay under it. Values above the number of listed enemies have no extra effect.

GenType.Wiki: How the generator is started. Automatic: it spawns on its own. Starts Disabled: like Automatic, but stays off until EMEVD Set Generator State enables it. Script Invoked: it only spawns when EMEVD Invoke Enemy Generator runs (the interval is skipped). Any value other than 2 or 3 acts as Automatic.

LimitNum.Wiki: The most enemies this generator spawns over its lifetime; once reached it stops. The enemies present at map load don't count. -1 for no limit; 0 means it never spawns.

MinGenNum.Wiki: The fewest enemies spawned in one batch; the generator spawns one enemy at a time, waiting the Spawn Delay between them. The batch is cut short so the alive count never passes Maximum Alive Count, and when no enemy is dead there is no batch. 0 can roll an empty batch.

MaxGenNum.Wiki: The most enemies spawned in one batch; the batch size is a whole number picked between the minimum and this value, both included. If this is not above the minimum, the minimum is always used.

MinInterval.Wiki: The shortest wait in seconds before a batch, once an enemy is dead. A new random wait between the minimum and maximum is picked after each batch. 0 and 0 spawn as soon as the generator notices a death (it checks every 1 to 2 seconds).

MaxInterval.Wiki: The longest wait in seconds before a batch. See Batch Interval: Minimum.

InitialSpawnCount.Wiki: How many of the listed enemies, counted from the first slot, are present where they are placed when the map loads. The rest are held back until the generator spawns them; held-back enemies are always spawned before dead ones are revived. 0 means every enemy waits for the generator.

MinSpawnDelay.Wiki: The shortest delay in seconds between two spawns of the same batch; the first spawn of a batch is immediate. 0 and 0 spawn the whole batch at once.

MaxSpawnDelay.Wiki: The longest delay in seconds between two spawns of the same batch. See Spawn Delay: Minimum.

SpawnRegionNames.Wiki: A region an enemy can appear at (8 slots). The regions are used in turn, starting after the one used last; a region with one of this generator's live enemies inside it is skipped, and if all are taken that spawn is lost (the batch still counts it). The enemy is warped to the region's position and faces the region's rotation.

SpawnPartNames.Wiki: An enemy this generator controls (32 slots). The generator does not create copies: it revives and moves these enemies, so the number of listed enemies is the most it can ever have alive. Each spawn picks a held-back enemy first (in slot order), otherwise the dead enemy farthest from the player.
